question.questionText: Unless we _______ throwing garbage into the river, it will be polluted.
question.explanationHtml:
Detailed Explanation:
The blank comes after 'unless', which is a conditional word. In conditional sentences with 'unless', we use the present simple tense to talk about a possible situation and its result. The correct structure is: Unless + subject + present simple, ...
  • A. won't stop (verb (future simple negative)): 'won't stop' is the future simple negative form. In conditional sentences with 'unless', we do not use the future tense in the 'unless' clause.
  • B. stop (verb (present simple)): 'stop' is the present simple form, which is correct for the 'unless' clause.
  • C. will stop (verb (future simple)): 'will stop' is the future simple form. We do not use 'will' after 'unless' in this type of conditional sentence.
  • D. don't stop (verb (present simple negative)): 'don't stop' is the present simple negative. However, 'unless' already means 'if not', so using 'don't' would create a double negative, which is incorrect.
Related structure or vocabulary: Unless + present simple, ...: This is a type 1 conditional sentence used to talk about real or possible situations in the present or future.
question.explanationViHtml:
Giải thích chi tiết:
Chỗ trống nằm sau 'unless', đây là từ dùng trong câu điều kiện. Trong câu điều kiện với 'unless', chúng ta sử dụng thì hiện tại đơn để nói về một tình huống có thể xảy ra và kết quả của nó. Cấu trúc đúng là: Unless + chủ ngữ + hiện tại đơn, ...
  • A. won't stop (động từ (tương lai đơn phủ định)): 'won't stop' là thì tương lai đơn phủ định. Trong câu điều kiện với 'unless', chúng ta không dùng thì tương lai trong mệnh đề 'unless'.
  • B. stop (động từ (hiện tại đơn)): 'stop' là thì hiện tại đơn, phù hợp với mệnh đề 'unless'.
  • C. will stop (động từ (tương lai đơn)): 'will stop' là thì tương lai đơn. Không dùng 'will' sau 'unless' trong loại câu điều kiện này.
  • D. don't stop (động từ (hiện tại đơn phủ định)): 'don't stop' là thì hiện tại đơn phủ định. Tuy nhiên, 'unless' đã mang nghĩa 'nếu không', nên dùng thêm 'don't' sẽ tạo thành phủ định kép, không đúng ngữ pháp.
Cấu trúc và từ vựng: Unless + hiện tại đơn, ...: Đây là câu điều kiện loại 1 dùng để nói về tình huống thực tế hoặc có thể xảy ra ở hiện tại hoặc tương lai.

Tạm dịch: Trừ khi chúng ta dừng việc vứt rác xuống sông, nếu không nó sẽ bị ô nhiễm.

question.questionText: She is too weak; she can't sit up and talk to you.

choices.text: If she isn't too weak, she can sit up and talk to you.
choices.raw: A. If she isn't too weak, she can sit up and talk to you.

choices.text: If she weren't too weak, she could sit up and talk to you.
choices.raw: B. If she weren't too weak, she could sit up and talk to you.

choices.text: If she hadn't been too weak, she could sit up and talk to you.
choices.raw: C. If she hadn't been too weak, she could sit up and talk to you.

choices.text: If she wasn't too weak, she can sit up and talk to you.
choices.raw: D. If she wasn't too weak, she can sit up and talk to you.

question.explanationHtml:
Detailed Explanation:
The sentence 'She is too weak; she can't sit up and talk to you.' expresses a present unreal situation: because she is too weak, she cannot sit up and talk. To rewrite this using a conditional sentence, we use the second conditional (If + past simple, ... would/could + base verb) to talk about unreal or hypothetical situations in the present.
  • A. If she isn't too weak, she can sit up and talk to you. (sentence): This is a first conditional sentence (If + present simple, ... will/can + base verb), used for real and possible situations in the present or future. However, the original sentence describes an unreal situation, so this is incorrect.
  • B. If she weren't too weak, she could sit up and talk to you. (sentence): This is a second conditional sentence (If + past simple, ... would/could + base verb), used for unreal or hypothetical situations in the present. This matches the meaning of the original sentence.
  • C. If she hadn't been too weak, she could sit up and talk to you. (sentence): This is a third conditional sentence (If + past perfect, ... would/could have + past participle), used for unreal situations in the past. The original sentence is about the present, so this is incorrect.
  • D. If she wasn't too weak, she can sit up and talk to you. (sentence): This mixes the past simple with 'can', which is not grammatically correct for conditional sentences. The correct form should be 'could' instead of 'can'.
Related structure or vocabulary: Second conditional: If + past simple, ... would/could + base verb. Used to talk about unreal or hypothetical situations in the present.

  • B. If she weren't too weak, she could sit up and talk to you. (câu): Đây là câu điều kiện loại 2 (If + quá khứ đơn, ... would/could + động từ nguyên mẫu), dùng cho tình huống không có thật hoặc giả định ở hiện tại. Đáp án này phù hợp với ý nghĩa của câu gốc.

question.explanationHtml:
Detailed Explanation:
The sentence 'I don't have enough money with me now; otherwise I will buy that coat.' is a conditional sentence expressing an unreal situation in the present. The speaker does not have enough money, so he/she cannot buy the coat. To rewrite this sentence using the correct conditional form, we use the second conditional: If + past simple, ... would + base verb. This structure is used to talk about unreal or hypothetical situations in the present.
  • A. If I had enough money with me now, I wouldn't buy that coat. (Conditional sentence): This choice uses the correct conditional structure, but the meaning is incorrect. 'Wouldn't buy' means the speaker would not buy the coat even if they had enough money, which is not the intended meaning.
  • B. If I had enough money with me now, I would buy that coat. (Conditional sentence): This choice uses the correct second conditional structure and matches the intended meaning: If the speaker had enough money, they would buy the coat.
  • C. If I didn't have enough money with me now, I would buy that coat. (Conditional sentence): This choice is incorrect because it suggests that not having enough money would allow the speaker to buy the coat, which is illogical.
  • D. If I didn't have enough money with me now, I wouldn't buy that coat. (Conditional sentence): This choice is incorrect because it implies the speaker currently has enough money, which contradicts the original sentence.
Related structure or vocabulary: Second conditional: If + past simple, ... would + base verb. Used for unreal or hypothetical situations in the present.

  • I were (verb (past simple, subjunctive mood)): 'If I were you' is correct. 'Were' is the past simple form used in the second conditional for all subjects, including 'I', to express unreal or hypothetical situations.
